chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Abu Hamza and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is goodness for you in my life and goodness for you in my death.'
So it was said, 'O Messenger of Allah! As for your life, we have known (that). But what is for us in your passing away?'
He said: 'As for my life, then indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: “And it was not for Allah to punish them while you are among them”.'
And as for my passing away, your deeds will be presented to me, so I will seek forgiveness for you.'
ai.seo_question: What is the benefit for believers in the Prophet's death?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the concept of *al-Hadhr al-Mawjood* (the presence of the Prophet) after death, a key tenet in Shia theology, asserting that the Prophet’s soul remains active in receiving the deeds of the Ummah. While his physical presence during life served as a divine shield against punishment (referencing Surah Al-Anfal), his posthumous intercession (*Shafa'ah*) continues to benefit believers through his supplication for their forgiveness.
